records.evidence: Fixed post-setup sleep assumes ten RTC seconds fit within ten wall seconds; registered legal 17 kHz LSI delays the callback, and Phase 1 replay confirmed the flip in Renode.
records.subject: rtc_alarm_callback

records.evidence: The 15 s calendar-arrival bound is below approximately 18.8 s for ten RTC seconds at registered legal 17 kHz LSI with a nominal 32 kHz prescaler.
records.snippet: zassert_true(elapsed_ms <= 15000, "RTC did not reach the alarm time within 15 seconds");
records.subject: rtc_alarm_callback-r04

records.evidence: Unbounded polling of sleep_started_ms has no synchronization and never yields to a lower-priority worker under this configuration; nominal run times out.
records.subject: sleep-r04

records.evidence: A 100 ms fixed delay stands in for observing that the worker entered sleep; nominal early completion is indirect evidence, but the delay itself has no registered scheduling bound.
records.subject: sleep-r01

records.evidence: A fixed 20 ms settle period is used to claim no later duplicate handler invocation; the intended observation horizon is not specified.
records.subject: workq-r05

records.evidence: callback_count is modified by a timer expiry callback and read as plain shared state after status_sync; ordering and compiler visibility need deeper review.

records.evidence: k_sem_count_get follows synchronous irq_offload completion, so the assertion does not assume asynchronous ISR arrival.
